A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ROMBRL research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial formatting changes.

before.justification: v2 reports original evaluations on twelve D4RL MuJoCo tasks and three simulated Tokamak tracking tasks, including numerical comparisons and training curves.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds baseline evaluations, gradient-update ablations, sensitivity tests, higher-noise experiments, and computational measurements.

M1.justification: The constrained maximin objective, Stackelberg updates, Fisher/Woodbury approximations, and Algorithms 1–2 remain unchanged. Appendix J retains the gradient masks, advantage estimates, truncated rollouts, and replay-buffer procedure. The new ablations test existing components rather than introduce a revised method.

E1.justification: The main MuJoCo and Tokamak coverage is retained. v3 adds 10% deployment-noise tests across Hopper datasets and includes 20% noise in the Hopper-medium-replay sensitivity study. Clean and 5% conditions already appeared in v2. The computational study calls its datasets '-expert' without clearly distinguishing expert from medium-expert data.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds RORL, TRACER, and RFQI to the five retained baselines, substantially broadening comparison against dedicated robust model-free methods. RORL also joins the clean/noisy comparison. The Tokamak comparator set, including BAMCTS, is unchanged between v2 Table 2 and v3 Table 3.

E3.justification: v3 introduces controlled comparisons of three update rules, five uncertainty-radius values at three noise levels, a four-by-two learning-rate grid, and runtime/peak-memory profiling. Table 2 adds percentage performance drop as a metric. These are new evaluation designs; the retained main benchmarks still specify 5% noise and averaging over the final 100 learning epochs.

E4.justification: v2 contains no corresponding component ablations or hyperparameter studies. v3 Section 6.3 compares naive alternating, unconstrained Stackelberg, and constrained Stackelberg updates. Appendix L tests uncertainty-radius sensitivity and learning-rate separation, while Appendix N adds stronger-noise robustness comparisons. These substantially expand diagnostic evidence about the method.

E5.justification: Appendix M newly states that all results use five independent seeds, whereas v2 specifies three and v3 Tables 1, 3, and 6 still specify three. This changes run-count reporting but does not reliably establish an actual increase in runs. Mean/standard-deviation reporting, Cohen's d, and omission of confidence intervals from training curves are retained.

E6.justification: All shared Table 1 score/standard-deviation pairs and Tokamak table values are unchanged. Added comparator results move ROMBRL from second to third on Walker2d-medium. New Figure 3 reports returns of 57.2, 62.1, and 79.4 for the three update rules; Appendices L–N add sensitivity, higher-noise, runtime, and memory results. These are added findings rather than improved scores for the retained experiments.

T1.justification: The suboptimality bounds, tabular and Gaussian results, mathematical assumptions, and derivations in Appendices A–J are retained. Writing the uncertainty set using KL notation and separately numbering previously inline matrix definitions are equivalent restatements, not new theory or corrected proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the principal method, theory, and robustness claims. Introduction contribution (4) now explicitly distinguishes state-of-the-art noisy performance from clean-setting competitiveness and claims clean-setting superiority over RAMBO, refining the earlier general top-performance statement.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive interpretations of clean-performance versus robustness tradeoffs, attributes ablation gains to constraint-response dynamics, links uncertainty-radius choice to disturbance strength, and discusses computational overhead. Appendix L also claims learning-rate separation is necessary, although Figure 5 reports 83.2 at equal learning rates of 10^-3, limiting that interpretation.

D1.justification: New Appendix M discloses an uncertainty radius of 10 for the main configuration, MOBILE-derived architectural settings, OfflineRL-Kit baseline defaults, and reuse of Walker2d-medium-expert hyperparameters for Tokamak. Appendix N specifies V100-SXM2-32GB hardware for profiling. These are additional disclosures, not evidence that existing experiments were reconfigured; complete numerical configurations and usable repository references remain incomplete.

R1.justification: v3 adds the RORL and TRACER references, removes Shi and Chi (2024), and replaces the blanket non-scalability discussion with distinctions among practical robust model-free approaches. It expands the comparison with RAMBO around alternating updates, implicit model responses, and conservatism while retaining the central Stackelberg novelty positioning.

P1.justification: The introduction, contribution list, and experimental discussion receive targeted rewrites. Section 6.3 and Appendices L–N are added, affiliations change, and an impact statement replaces the acknowledgments. The existing section sequence and most method and proof prose are retained.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from one-column to two-column layout. Table 1 and Figure 1 expand, and v3 adds three diagnostic figures plus clean/noisy-summary, computational-cost, and higher-noise tables. The original training-curve graphics are unchanged but move to Appendix N as Figures 6–7; the Tokamak illustration and state/action table are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2's benchmark-focused experiments, v3 better tests the distinctive gradient update, includes robust model-free competitors, and documents sensitivity and computational costs. These strengthen the paper's empirical support. The net gain is limited by contradictory three-versus-five-seed reporting and an overstated learning-rate conclusion: Figure 5 retains a score of 83.2 at equal 10^-3 rates despite claiming collapse whenever the policy learning rate meets or exceeds the model rate.
